page: Microsoft Azure D32d_v5 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 1229 GB local SSD for high-speed temporary storage.

Benchmark results place the D32d_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 13741.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 36837.52. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 134.84 GB/sec and a write speed of 63.71 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, it demonstrates strong performance in text generation using small (135M) language models at 304.37 tokens/sec, though performance drops significantly to a poor rating of 2.3 tokens/sec when running large (70B) models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32d_v5 offers a balanced resource density, combining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with substantial local SSD storage. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the premium of memory-optimized tiers. It is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate-scale data processing tasks.
